title: Front Door Check Arm Removal and Installation
introduction:
The check arm spans the gap between the door and body, but much of its assembly hides inside the door. That little link has a surprisingly large backstage crew: the trim panel, its wiring and latch cable, and the front watershield all stand between you and removal.

I use the drawings to distinguish the exposed body attachment from the assembly’s door-mounted fasteners. The instructions below retain the removal order and explain the linked trim-access work. Reinstallation reverses that order; the torque values beside removal steps apply when those fasteners go back.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts inside the door. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Body Repair Health and Safety and General Precautions](#/document/G1693182) before starting.

items.name: Equipment for access and refitting
items.detail: Have a trim-removal lever for the window-switch bezel and torque equipment suitable for the attachment specifications given here and in the linked trim-panel procedure. The switch illustration shows a trim lever; it does not specify a tool size.

items.name: Applicability and references
items.detail: The [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) procedure shows LHD and the RH door; RHD and the LH door are similar. Its required nested reference is [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936), section 501-11 Glass, Frames and Mechanisms, Removal and Installation. That switch procedure shows LHD, with RHD similar, and illustrates the LH side, with the RH side similar.

items.name: Expose the trim-panel fasteners
items.detail: After removing the check-arm body bolt as directed below, remove the small cover inside the interior door-handle recess, then remove the upper trim-panel bolt. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Next, use the trim lever to lift the window-control switch and bezel assembly from the armrest, disengaging its retaining clips, and disconnect the switch electrical connector. Remove the center trim-panel bolt exposed in the armrest opening; its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Then remove the lower retainers along the underside of the panel; their installation torque is 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Leave the window switch attached to its bezel for this check-arm job; separating the switch is a different replacement task.

items.name: Free the panel around its edges
items.detail: Work in the linked procedure’s order. At the rear upper portion, move the panel away from the door to disengage the clip near the upper rear edge, followed by the pin-type retainers below it. At the rear and lower portion, release the pin-type retainer near the lower rear corner, then the clip near the bottom beside the large speaker. At the front edge, release the lower pin-type retainer above the large speaker, followed by the remaining pin-type attachments farther up that edge. Pull these portions away from the door as their attachments disengage.

items.name: Disconnect the panel without leaving the handle tethered
items.detail: Lift the panel up and out of the door. Disconnect its electrical connectors if equipped. Looking at the back of the panel, locate the latch cable behind the interior handle. Slide the cable-sheath fitting out through the opening in its retaining bracket, then detach the cable end from the handle. These are separate attachments: freeing the sheath fitting allows the cable end to be disconnected. Remove the panel once these connections are free.

items.name: Restore the cable, wiring and panel attachments
items.detail: Transfer parts as necessary. Reverse the panel-removal sequence: reconnect the latch-cable end to the interior handle, then seat the cable-sheath fitting in its retaining bracket. Reconnect the panel electrical connectors if equipped. Move the panel in and down to engage its upper mounting edge. Re-engage the front-edge pin-type attachments, the lower/rear clip and pin-type retainer, and the rear upper pin-type retainers and clip in reverse release order. Refit the lower retainers and center bolt, reconnect the window-switch electrical connector and seat the switch/bezel clips, then refit the upper bolt and its cover. Use the respective installation torques given in the access instructions. See [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600).

edits.text: NOTE: The removal steps also include details needed for installation.
edits.why: I read the torque callouts before starting so the refitting requirements are already clear when the parts come off.

edits.text: NOTE: The LH side is shown; the RH side is similar.
edits.why: Use the illustrated attachment relationships for the opposite door while accounting for the mirrored layout.

edits.text:
Remove the bolt securing the exposed end of the check arm to the body-side bracket in the door opening.
Installation torque: 18 lb.ft (25 Nm).
edits.why: The highlighted bolt is at the outer end of the arm spanning the door-to-body gap. Removing it disconnects that end before work moves inside the door. Control the door by hand before removing this bolt and throughout the work while the check arm is disconnected. Keep it from swinging freely or opening beyond its normal travel; the check arm cannot limit it while detached.

edits.text:
Remove the front door trim panel using the access sequence described above.
Refer to: [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The trim panel covers the interior access needed later. Its fasteners, edge attachments, electrical connectors and interior-handle cable must all be freed in sequence; the cable is a tether, not an invitation to pull harder.

edits.text:
Remove the nuts securing the check-arm assembly to the front edge of the door, above and below the arm’s mounting opening.
Installation torque: 106 lb.in (12 Nm).
edits.why: The drawing identifies the door-side attachments beside the wiring connection. With these nuts removed, the assembly is no longer secured to the door at that mounting face.

edits.text: Remove the front watershield covering the interior access opening near the hinge side of the door.
edits.why: This is the small highlighted shield in the drawing. Removing it opens the route used to withdraw the check-arm assembly.

edits.text: Move the check-arm assembly clear of its mounting opening in the front edge of the door, then withdraw it through the interior access opening.
edits.why: I use the paired views to connect the mounting face with the hidden assembly inside the door. The assembly comes out through the opened interior access route after its exposed arm and door-side attachments have been freed.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: position the check-arm assembly inside the door and engage its mounting opening, refit the front watershield, reinstall the door-side nuts, reinstall the front door trim panel, and finally reconnect the arm to the body-side bracket with its bolt. Tighten the check-arm fasteners to the installation torques given in their removal steps.
edits.why: Reversing the sequence restores the concealed assembly and watershield before the trim closes access. The trim-completion instructions above distinguish reconnecting the handle-cable end from seating its sheath fitting, then restore the wiring, panel attachments and switch assembly. After every attachment, cable and connector is restored and tools are clear, keep the parked car restrained and gently open and close the door by its handle, checking normal check-arm restraint and latch engagement without forcing it. Confirm the interior handle releases the latch normally. To check the disturbed window connection, bring the valid key inside. From confirmed ignition OFF, press and release START/STOP with both pedals released to select engine-off ON; if already ON, leave it ON. Keep children and pets away and all hands and objects clear of the glass. Press the window switch to open the window and lift it to close, confirming normal response without testing or overriding bounce-back. Finish from known ON by pressing and releasing START/STOP with both pedals released to select OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before any connector reinspection. These are ordinary assembly checks, not electrical diagnosis or door alignment. Stop and correct abnormal movement, retention or operation before driving.

editorialRevision.scope: Remove unrelated switch replacement branches; add stationary known-state preparation, controlled unrestrained door handling and owner-backed ordinary window completion. Primary actions/torques unchanged. Pending independent incremental approval.
